title: Set up ReRev Comms Review
intro: ReRev Comms Review is a small web page that shows your marketing campaigns, audiences and content ideas in one place. It is a static site. It has no server and no database. The page reads JSON data files from your own GitHub repository. It is hosted on GitHub Pages. A shared password screen guards the page. This wizard helps you copy the tool to your own GitHub account and make it use your own data. The tool starts with sample data from ReRev Labs. You must replace that data with your own.

variables.label: Your business name
variables.help: The name that you want to show for your team.

variables.label: Your GitHub username
variables.help: The name in your GitHub profile address.
variables.pattern_error: Use letters, numbers and hyphens only. Maximum 39 characters.

variables.label: New repository name
variables.help: The name for your copy of the tool.
variables.pattern_error: Use letters, numbers, dots, hyphens and underscores only.

variables.label: Your site address
variables.help: GitHub Pages builds this address from your username and repository name.

variables.label: Your data address
variables.help: The page reads data files from this address.

steps.title: Check what you need
steps.instructions: You need one free GitHub account. You need a web browser. You do not need to pay for anything. You do not need to install software. Read the first paragraph of this page again if you want to know what the tool does. Then tick the box.
steps.verify_hint: Open github.com and confirm that you are signed in.

steps.title: Enter your public values
steps.instructions: Enter your business name. Enter your GitHub username. Choose a name for your new repository. This wizard shows these values in later steps so that you do not type them again. Do not enter a password here.

steps.title: Get your own copy of the code
steps.instructions: Open the template repository link that ReRev Labs sent you. Click the green button named Use this template, or click Fork. Choose your account as the owner. Enter {{repo_name}} as the name. Make the repository Public. GitHub Pages needs a public repository on a free account. Click Create repository.
steps.verify_hint: Open https://github.com/{{github_username}}/{{repo_name}}. You must see the files index.html and campaigns.json.

steps.title: Turn on GitHub Pages
steps.instructions: In your repository, click Settings. Click Pages in the left menu. Under Build and deployment, set Source to Deploy from a branch. Set Branch to main and the folder to / (root). Click Save. Wait one to two minutes for the first build.
steps.verify_hint: Open {{pages_url}}. You must see a password screen.

steps.title: Point the page to your own data
steps.instructions: The page file has two address lines and one password line. They still point to the ReRev Labs copy. Change them now. In your repository, open index.html. Click the pencil icon to edit. Use Ctrl+F to find the lines that start with const REPO_RAW and const PAGES_BASE. Replace the address inside the quotes with the values below. Keep the quotes.
steps.verify_hint: Search index.html for keyona-rerev. Some links, such as the feedback link, may still use the old name. Replace each with {{github_username}}/{{repo_name}}. Do not commit yet.

steps.title: Set your own page password
steps.instructions: The page has a built-in password. It is a shared gate only. It is not strong security. Anyone who views the page source can read it. Do not use it to protect private or sensitive data. Do not reuse a password from another account. In index.html, find the line that starts with const SITE_PASSWORD. Replace the text inside the quotes with a new password that you choose. Never share this password in a public place. Then scroll down and click Commit changes.
steps.checkbox_label: I set my own password and committed the change.
steps.verify_hint: Wait one minute. Open {{pages_url}}. Enter your new password. The old password must not work.

steps.title: Remove the sample data
steps.instructions: The data files hold ReRev Labs sample content. Replace each file with your own content. Open each file in your repository and click the pencil icon. The files are campaigns.json, audiences.json, initiatives.json, content_formats.json, pipeline.json and rejections.json. Keep the same structure of each file. Change only the values. Delete the folder named assets if you do not need the sample email template. Commit each change. Remember that your repository is public. Do not put private contact details in these files.
steps.checkbox_label: I replaced the sample data with my own.
steps.verify_hint: Open each file. You must not see any ReRev Labs names or contacts.

steps.title: Run your first test
steps.instructions: Open {{pages_url}}. Enter your password. Check that the Home, Campaigns, Audiences and Initiatives tabs load. Check that your own data shows. If you see an error or empty lists, press Ctrl+Shift+R to reload. Then check that the data files in your repository are valid JSON.
steps.checkbox_label: My data shows on the page.
steps.verify_hint: {{business_name}} data must show in the tabs. The page must not show any ReRev Labs data.

steps.title: How to update later
steps.instructions: To change your content, edit the JSON data files in your repository. The page reads the newest data each time that it loads. To get new versions of the tool, open the version history page. Compare your version with the newest version. Follow the upgrade steps that the history page shows. Keep your own address lines and password when you update index.html.
steps.checkbox_label: I know where to find the version history.
steps.verify_hint: Open the history link on this wizard. You must see a list of versions.
